item.lead: The character script cut its text at ninety percent with two slices. The GPT-2 byte-pair script makes the same cut, so put the two side by side. Look for what stays identical and what changes. The encoder is the only part that should differ, and with it the number of ids each piece produces.
item.follow: The cut is the same in both scripts: the text is split at int(n*0.9) before encoding. Only the encoder changes. For characters, id counts equal slice lengths. For GPT-2 byte pairs, common character runs merge, so the same text gives far fewer ids: 301,966 for training and 36,059 for validation. Next: why the held-back tenth must never be seen during training.
